content: Hello  @everyone  👋! There is an online community that might be of interest called Code.AI, a community dedicated for all things related to AI for code. In this community we not only discuss deep learning or code generation, we also discuss things like evolutionary computation and code documentation! It is a great place to find fellow like-minded researchers and developers, build a team of collaborators, find a project to work on, or brainstorm project and research ideas! We also do community events like paper reading club sessions, community research projects (e.g. https://github.com/CodedotAl/gpt-code-clippy/wiki), and are planning for more community events like podcasts and blogposts! Our community would also love to hear more about all the wonderful work and interests you guys have! If you are interested please join us using this link: https://discord.gg/68NZFfxHxD !

From: Andrew Pangia <apangia@charlotte.edu>
Date: Fri, Feb 2, 2024 at 4:28 PM
Subject: TAIMing AI Seminar 2-6-24
To: Taufiquar Khan <taufiquar.khan@charlotte.edu>

Dear all,

This coming Tuesday, February 6, 12-1pm, in Fretwell 206, we will be holding the first seminar for the Center for Trustworthy Artificial Intelligence in Model risk management (TAIMing AI). Our first talk will be by guest speaker Dr. Rahul Singh of Wells Fargo Bank. The title and abstract, as well as a brief bio are below. Chairs, please forward this to your mailing lists, and see you there!

Title: Large Language Models and Generative AI: Deep dive into the landscape and applications


Abstract: 

Generative AI refers to the creation of new content in various forms, including images, videos, and text. Recent breakthroughs in generative AI has happened on the backbone of large language models (LLMs). LLMs such as DALL-E and ChatGPT have garnered widespread attention due to their versatility in generating content for diverse queries. These innovations have given rise to numerous applications, and researchers continue to explore new possibilities. At the core of generative AI lies the transformer architecture, which boasts millions to trillions of parameters and requires training on vast datasets. This process is complex and involves multi-step training methods, including language modeling, instruction fine-tuning, and Reinforcement Learning with Human Feedback (RLHF). Our presentation will delve into these elements and examine the evolving landscape of generative AI, highlighting recent advancements within our group and how we leverage these technologies for our applications.

content:
If you’re interested in getting involved in research at the Charlotte Machine Learning Lab, there’s a great opportunity for Spring 2025 through the Office of Undergraduate Research (OUR)! There are some exciting projects available, including four from Dr. Kuemmerle and two in the machine learning field from Dr. Bunescu. More details about the projects can be found here: [Research Projects Spring 2025](https://charlotteml.github.io/news/office-of-undergraduate-research-spring-2025)

If you’re new to research and don’t know where to start, here’s a quick guide on how to get involved:

    1.    Step 1: Don’t overthink it—just start!
    2.    Step 2: Find professors you’re interested in working with. Check out the CCI faculty pages or literally knock on some doors to introduce yourself.
    3.    Step 3: Research their work. Make sure you know what they do before reaching out.
    4.    Step 4: Schedule a meeting. Look at their Google Calendar and propose at least 3 meeting times to make it easier for them. During the meeting, ask them how you can learn more about their research and if they have any resources to share.
    5.    Step 5: Follow up in 2-3 weeks. After learning more about their work, reach out again.
    6.    Step 6: Ask about positions! Once you’re familiar with their research, see if they have any open spots for you to get involved.

Feel free to check out the application process for the OUR programs [here](https://our.charlotte.edu/programs/academic-year-programs#application-process ): Application Process.

Good luck and happy researching!  Please react with 🚨 if you are thinking about applying! 

# Deadline October 22nd https://our.charlotte.edu/programs/academic-year-programs/
